newsitem.title: USA: Coleman results hurt by acquisition, other charges.
newsitem.headline: Coleman results hurt by acquisition, other charges.

text.p: Coleman Co. Inc. Monday reported a loss for the fourth quarter, with results affected by bad weather during the camping season and costs associated with acquisitions, restructuring and other charges.
"We at Coleman recognise that 1996 was a difficult and disappointing year. However, the fundamentals of Coleman's business are solid, and its growth prospects are strong," said Chairman Jerry Levin.

The company reported a net loss after restructuring and other charges of $35.9 million, or 67 cents per share, for the fourth quarter compared with a net loss of $9.8 million or 18 cents per share in the fourth quarter of 1995.
Sales reached $224.4 million, a 20 percent increase from $186.5 million in the same period a year earlier.
Bad weather during camping season in North America and the weak economy in Japan both hurt results.

For the year, the company reported a net loss after restructuring and other charges of $41.9 million, or 79 cents per share, compared with a net profit of $39.3 million, or 74 cents per share in 1995.
Sales rose nearly 31 percent to $1.22 billion compared with $933.6 million for 1995.
Restructuring and other charges included the costs of integrating France's Camping Gaz into the company and charges in connection with litigation.
Coleman, based in Golden, Colo., manufactures and distributes products for camping, leisure, hardware and home safety and security.
Coleman stock was up 25 cents at $13.50 on the New York Stock Exchange in afternoon trading.
